business_scope.primary_industry_name: Franchise Licensing and Syrups Supply Chain for Bubble Tea Chains

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (province of Alberta within a Federal_State; common law supplemented by federal and provincial statutory overlay)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CUSMA (United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement), in force 1 July 2020
CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership), in force for Canada 30 December 2018
CETA (Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement), provisionally applied since 21 September 2017
Canada–China FIPA (Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement), in force 1 October 2014
Canada–Korea Free Trade Agreement, in force 1 January 2015
Canada–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, in force 1 April 2021

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, Part 2 (Limited Partnerships) ss. 51-88; Partnership Regulation, Alta Reg 124/2004; Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (governing the corporate general partner)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (RegistryXpress / eCorp online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) together with NUANS name search report and registered office consent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for Alberta limited partnerships; capital contributions are established contractually in the limited partnership agreement and may be satisfied by cash, property or services. No escrow account is mandated by the Partnership Act; franchise royalty funds may be escrowed only under the franchise or supply agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner approves and adopts the Limited Partnership Agreement for Boba Tea Global Franchise LP (the Partnership), a limited partnership registered under the Partnership Act (Alberta), and accepts the limited partners' capital contributions as recorded in the contribution register. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be and is hereby fixed at the Alberta address named in the Declaration of Limited Partnership. RESOLVED FURTHER, that CEO, CFO and Corporate Secretary are appointed, each authorized to execute formation filings, deal with the Alberta Corporate Registry, open bank accounts, and engage counsel and tax advisors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via accredited NUANS service providers or Service Alberta counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three to five proposed partnership names incorporating the mandatory legal element 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.'. File the NUANS name search request, receive the search report, and retain a certified copy for submission with Form LP-1. Confirm that the chosen name is distinguishable from existing corporate names in the Alberta registry.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search request form
Three to five proposed names ranked in order of preference
Authorizing resolution of the proposed general partner
Name search fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A refused name may be re-submitted under a different name, or a written objection and reconsideration request may be filed with the Registrar of Companies within thirty days of the refusal notice, citing acquired distinctiveness and supporting search evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Authorization of Partnership Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External legal counsel qualified in Alberta; witnessed execution, notarization optional
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement covering capital accounts, allocations, distributions, transfer restrictions and authority of the general partner; complete Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1); obtain the corporate general partner's board resolutions; execute the agreement with witnessed signatures and certify all copies.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement (final draft)
Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) signed by each general partner
Board resolution of the corporate general partner
Consent to act as registered office (Form AR-1 or registry equivalent)
Certified copy of the general partner's certificate of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficient signature blocks or inconsistent capital schedules are cured by amending the schedules and re-executing the agreement; a corrected resolution supersedes any prior inconsistent authorization and is filed with the partnership records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (RegistryXpress / eCorp); paper counter for postal applications
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit Form LP-1 together with the NUANS search report and prescribed fee. The Registrar issues a Certificate of Registration confirming the limited partnership's registration date and corporate access number (CAN). Verify registry data within thirty days of issuance and file any correction promptly.
required_dossiers: Execution copy of Form LP-1 Declaration of Limited Partnership
Original NUANS name search report (issued within 90 days)
Registered office consent and Alberta address for service
Payment of CAD 100 registration fee (USD 75 equivalent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the Registrar issues a deficiency notice; the filer must submit corrected documentation within 60 days or re-file. A rectification order may also be sought under s. 78 of the Partnership Act for clerical errors appearing in the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Number program; WCB Alberta; Alberta provincial tax authorities for the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit CRA Form RC1 to obtain a Business Number for the partnership; select GST/HST, payroll and import/export accounts as applicable. Register the corporate general partner for Alberta corporate income tax; create the WCB Alberta account and obtain employer registration confirmation.
required_dossiers: CRA RC1 business number application
Certificate of Registration of the limited partnership
Certified copies of the general partner's incorporation documents
Officers' identification and authority documentation
Partnership bank account details or preliminary letter from financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CRA rejects an application only where identification is incomplete; remedy by submitting the missing authority documents or a corrected RC1. The applicant may also escalate within CRA's Business Window or file a service complaint under the Canada Revenue Agency Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Processing Facility and Franchise Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA), Safe Food for Canadians Act (SFCA) licensing; Alberta Health Services (AHS) Environmental Public Health
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the SFCA licence application for food processing covering syrup and tea beverage concentrate manufacture, with a validated HACCP plan, preventive control plan and recall procedure. Apply concurrently to AHS for a Public Health Operating Permit for the commissary and each franchised retail outlet; complete a pre-licensing inspection before the first production run.
required_dossiers: SFCA licence application and preventive control plan
HACCP plan and supporting monitoring forms
Facility floor plans and equipment specifications
Potable water quality testing results
Product recall and traceability procedure
AHS operating permit application for each premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A CFIA refusal will list non-conformities; submit a corrective action plan within 15 business days and request a re-inspection. Refusal may be appealed under s. 18 of the Safe Food for Canadians Act; an AHS permit denial may be cured through plan revisions and re-inspection with municipal health services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Development, Fire Safety and Occupational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal development authority; accredited municipality under the Safety Codes Council; Alberta OHS; WCB Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain development and building permits; upon construction completion, request a building occupancy inspection and fire safety inspection under the Alberta Fire Code; finalize the occupancy certificate; complete the OHS hazard assessment, WHMIS program, first-aid certification and WCB registration covering franchise staff.
required_dossiers: Development permit application
Building permit and stamped structural drawings
Fire safety inspection report under the Alberta Fire Code
Building occupancy certificate
Alberta OHS hazard assessment and WHMIS records
WCB Alberta registration confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal permit denials may be appealed to the Subdivision and Development Appeal Board (SDAB) within 21 days. Unresolved fire or building code deficiencies require corrective construction and a request for re-inspection; administrative review is available through the Safety Codes Council if statutory timelines are not met.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA); Alberta Health Services (AHS) Environmental Public Health; Alberta Environment and Protected Areas; municipal safety codes authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians Act Licence (food processing for syrup and tea beverage concentrate); Alberta Health Operating Permit (food establishment); Municipal Business Licence and Building Occupancy Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (EPEA) and municipal drainage/sewer utility
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration/notification tier; a full EIA report is not typically triggered for a syrups and tea concentrate manufacturing facility using food-grade inputs with low effluent volumes. Activity registration under the EPEA and municipal sewer use authorization are required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: municipal sewer bylaw limits such as BOD no greater than 300 mg/L, TSS no greater than 350 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.0, and oil/grease below 100 mg/L before sanitary sewer discharge. Emissions: minor VOC and odour sources must comply with municipal odour nuisance bylaws; no major combustion sources are anticipated. Waste handling: organic residues and packaging wastes are segregated and recycled or disposed through licensed carriers under the EPEA Waste Regulation; hazardous cleaning chemicals require manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by an accredited municipality under the Alberta Fire Code; structural load inspection and final building occupancy certificate; Alberta OHS clearance comprising hazard assessment, WHMIS training, first-aid certification and WCB workers' compensation registration; separate municipal business licence and exterior signage permit for each franchise outlet.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Federal Tax Authority and Portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian entities including Limited Partnerships obtain Business Number (BN) and GST/HST registration directly from CRA via online My Business Account portal. No foreign entity procedure applies as this is a domestic Canadian LP.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Limited partnerships are statutorily classified as pass-through entities under the Income Tax Act; no elective check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections available or required.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Registrants must file GST/HST returns electronically through the CRA's My Business Account system. Real-time reporting not mandated; compliance via periodic electronic filings and digital audit trails.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: GST is zero-rated on exports of goods and zero-rated supplies of services performed outside Canada. Eligibility requires proof of export or performance outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits may result in penalties of up to 200% of evaded tax for false statements or non-compliance; retrospective GST adjustments and potential criminal prosecution for fraudulent claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canadian Dollar (CAD) is a freely convertible currency for both capital and current account transactions under the Foreign Exchange Act. Profit remittances to non-resident partners are permitted without prior approval, subject only to exchange control reporting and beneficial ownership disclosure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds required for current account transactions. All export receipts must be reported to the Bank of Canada via the Canadian Survey of International Transactions or through authorized foreign exchange dealers. Capital account transactions involving non-residents require specific reporting but not surrender.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited viability for offshore digital EMIs due to Canadian anti-money laundering and foreign exchange reporting obligations under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC. Corporate clients must route cross-border transactions through regulated Tier 1 banks to ensure compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote KYC opening is permitted for eligible Alberta Limited Partnerships via video verification and electronic documentation. Directors and authorized signers may be required to attend in-person interviews for accounts above CAD 500,000 or with complex ownership structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening or adverse media hits on directors or partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified partnership agreement, beneficial ownership declaration, source-of-funds evidence, and board resolutions confirming legitimate business purpose

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Partnership agreement, list of partners with proof of non-resident status, and certified true copies of director identification

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections via SWIFT wire transfers using purpose code 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'. Verification requires supporting documentation including partnership agreement, capital contribution resolution, and proof of funds source. All transactions must be reported to the Bank of Canada.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements include SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers and issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit through correspondent banks. Trade settlements must reference underlying franchise royalty agreements or syrup supply contracts with proper invoicing and transfer pricing documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Limited Partnership Annual Return (recurring registration filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta / Registrar of Companies, Government of Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the limited partnership's registration anniversary each year (anniversary-based cycle; no fixed calendar date).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An administrative late-filing fee is assessed for returns submitted after the anniversary window; failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to administratively dissolve the LP. Reinstatement requires a formal revival application, settlement of all outstanding fees, and payment of restoration charges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 partner slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 5 months after the LP fiscal period-end (May 31 for a December 31 year-end); the return and slips share the same filing deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers the Income Tax Act s. 162(2.2) penalty: minimum CAD 100, up to CAD 25 per partner per month, to a maximum of CAD 2,500; each missing T5013 slip attracts a CAD 50 penalty; continued default may lead to prosecution and additional court-imposed fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Disclosure Document refresh and pre-sale delivery
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Delivered to each prospective franchisee; statutory oversight by the Alberta Securities Commission as administrator of the Alberta Franchises Act. No government registry filing is required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: A current disclosure document must be delivered no later than 14 days before franchise agreement execution; the franchisor must refresh the disclosure document annually and immediately upon any material change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficiencies trigger statutory rescission rights (including the 60-day rescission window for disclosure failures under s. 12 of the Franchises Act) and damages for misrepresentation; the LP as franchisor may also be exposed to franchisee fraud claims and litigation costs.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on an Alberta LP by the Partnership Act itself. A compulsory independent audit is triggered where (i) the partnership agreement or a financing/franchise agreement requires audited financial statements; (ii) the LP is consolidated into a group whose parent is a reporting issuer; or (iii) the corporate general partner is an ABCA corporation that has not validly waived the audit under s. 155 of the Business Corporations Act by unanimous shareholder consent.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS under the CPA Canada Handbook is required for publicly accountable enterprises; otherwise, Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is the default for a privately held LP. The selected framework must be consistent with the general partner's financial reporting and the franchise royalty revenue recognition policy.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not maintain a public UBO registry for limited partnerships. The LP must retain a statutory Register of Limited Partners at its Alberta registered office showing each limited partner's name, address, aggregate capital contribution, and profit entitlement. A transfer of a limited partnership interest is recognized only upon entry in the register; the general partner must reconcile contribution and distribution records annually and certify register accuracy in the LP annual return. For FINTRAC and anti-money-laundering purposes, beneficial-ownership and KYC records for each limited partner are re-verified on a risk-based annual cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (names, addresses, capital contributions, profit shares, transfer entries)
Register of General Partners and Capital Account Records
Minute Book of Partnership Resolutions and Consents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $150–$385 per year for a third-party Alberta registered office and corporate agent (typical market range CAD 200–CAD 520).
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $5,500–$18,500 per year for a mid-complexity franchise royalty LP with consolidated general-partner reporting (typical market range CAD 7,500–CAD 25,000).

stage_6.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII (Income Tax Act subsection 212(2) deems a dividend for non-resident partners' shares of Canadian-source partnership income; ordinary corporate dividends are also 25%)
stage_6.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form NR301 to the CRA before the payment date to apply the reduced treaty rate; obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the partner's residence jurisdiction and retain the applicable treaty article analysis. For Canada-US royalty payments, a Form W-8BEN-E is accepted as a basis for withholding at 10%; for Canada-China royalty and interest payments, the DTA rate is 10%. If excess was withheld, claim a refund through Form NR7 within two years. For Part I net-basis treatment of active business income of a non-resident partner with a Canadian permanent establishment, the partner files a non-resident T1/T2 return and invokes subsection 212(2.1) to remove the deemed dividend.
